claim.why_it_matters: The PDF prints 'PIC S9(7' with NO closing right parenthesis — verified by cropping and zooming the line; the adjacent COMMIT-FREQUENCY line on the same page correctly prints 'PIC S9(5)'. This is a typographical defect in ISO's own informative example. The transcription silently repairs it. Silent repair is the same class of error as silent loss: the transcription is supposed to reproduce the page, and a project that keeps a ledger of ISO's own defects cannot find this one because the markdown no longer shows it. It also hides the fact that the Annex D sample program as printed is not compilable source.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED after an adversarial attempt to refute it on every available ground; the claim quotes both sources accurately. (1) Rendered page 1053 at 300 dpi and 600 dpi via scripts/spec/page_workunit.py and scripts/render-spec-page.py. A full-width 600 dpi crop of the single raster row containing '03  WORK-QTY' shows that same row reading 'PIC S9(7' followed by blank space and then 'PACKED-DECIMAL.' — so the data-name and the defective PIC clause are bound to one physical line, not a reflow or wrap artifact. (2) Glyph-level zoom shows '(' and '7' rendering cleanly with nothing after the '7'. (3) Decisive quantitative check — an ink-column profile (pixels < 200 on 0-255 grayscale) over the three PACKED-DECIMAL lines at 600 dpi: the character cell at x=3191-3206 holds the ')' glyph with 32 dark pixels on the COMMIT-FREQUENCY line and 27 on the COMMIT-COUNT line, but has EXACTLY ZERO dark pixels on the WORK-QTY line. The ink runs on WORK-QTY jump from (3132,3166) — the digit '7' — straight to (3452,3493), the start of PACKED-DECIMAL. This is absence, not faintness. (4) Font/glyph-dropout by the rasterizer is ruled out: the ')' glyph renders correctly elsewhere on this very page in the same monospace font, at the same size, and at the identical x-column, on the two immediately adjacent lines. (5) The PDF text layer is obfuscated (get_text returns scrambled code points such as U+0200), which is the known property of this PDF that makes the raster the authoritative channel, so it could neither confirm nor contradict; character bounding boxes show a cell present at that position on all three lines, consistent with a SPACE having been typeset where the ')' belongs. (6) The markdown at specs/ISO_COBOL.md page-1053 line 24 does read 'PIC S9(7)'. (7) Context attribution in the claim is correct: page 1053 (printed folio 1023) sits in Annex D, headed '(informative)', section D.2.5 'Commit and rollback'. No refutation ground survives — the text is not present reflowed or on an adjacent line, the difference is not page-break furniture, wrapping, hyphenation or formatting, and neither source is misquoted.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as filed; two refinements. (a) Scope — this is a one-character divergence confined to an informative Annex D example, and the author's intent is unambiguously 'S9(7)' (the sibling COMMIT-COUNT item on the same page is declared PIC S9(7) and WORK-QTY is used interchangeably with it), so no normative rule and no compiler behavior depends on it; 'cosmetic' severity is right, and the value is purely ledger fidelity — recording an ISO typo, not a semantic loss. (b) The strongest form of the argument is one the claim did not make: the transcription is INCONSISTENT rather than uniformly normalizing. Eleven lines further down the same page the PDF misprints the DECLARATIVES header, placing the terminating period at the start of the following line as '. USER-FATAL-ERROR SECTION.', and the markdown reproduces that printing defect verbatim at line 43. So the same page shows the transcription faithfully preserving one ISO typo while silently repairing another. That inconsistency — not the missing parenthesis alone — is what makes the page unreliable as a defect ledger, since a reader cannot tell from the markdown which oddities are ISO's and which are the transcriber's. The claim's remark that the repair 'hides the fact that the Annex D sample program as printed is not compilable source' is true but should not be read as unique to this line: the sample as printed already fails to compile at the DECLARATIVES header, and that failure IS visible in the markdown.
